I found 4 accessibility defects on `fluxo.html`. The report was sent to `http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/submit` and accepted (HTTP 200, status "aceito", file `2026-09-17T23-35-57-sem-run1-177ec248.json`).

- `.link-opcao` | `wcag:2.4.7` | The 4 links under "Outras opções de identificação" show nothing when they get keyboard focus. The CSS rule `.link-opcao:focus, .link-opcao:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:none }` removes it. The page's other links and buttons show a dashed outline.
- `#cpf` | `wcag:3.3.1` | Submitting the empty form shows "Informe um CPF para continuar.", but the field isn't linked to that message: it has no `aria-invalid` or `aria-describedby`, and its border doesn't change.
- `.mensagem-erro-cpf` | `wcag:4.1.3` | Screen readers don't announce the error when it appears. It has no `role="alert"` or `aria-live`, and focus stays on the Continuar button.
- `.barra-recursos` | `wcag:1.4.10` | At 320 px wide the page scrolls sideways (content is 447 px wide). The header buttons don't wrap and the VLibras button ends up off-screen.

**What I tested:** Tab and focus on every control, the empty form, CPF "123" and a valid CPF, the "Alto Contraste" button, and a 320×640 window. I also measured text contrast: everything reaches at least 4.5:1.

**Left out as uncertain (noted in the report):**
- The form accepts "123" the same way as a valid CPF, with no error.
- "Alto Contraste" changes nothing visible.

This may be intentional in a prototype, so I didn't count either as a defect.

**Limitations:**
- No rules oracle or `scan_page` tool was available, so I did everything by hand.
- The `.mensagem-erro-cpf` selector only matches after submitting the empty form. The report lists that step.
